chunks: 5577 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Jaʿfar ibn Ḥanān, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who endowed the yield of his property for relatives of his from his father's side and relatives from his mother's side, and he made a bequest from that yield for a man and his descendants—between whom and him there was no kinship—of three hundred dirhams every year, and the remainder was to be divided among his relatives from his father and mother. He said: “It is permissible for the one for whom he made that bequest.”

I said: “What do you think if only five hundred dirhams come out from the yield of the land that he endowed?” He said: “Is it not in his bequest that the one for whom he made the bequest should be given from the yield three hundred dirhams, and the remainder be divided among his relatives from his father and mother?”
I said: “Yes.” He said: “His relatives have no right to take anything from the yield until they fully give the one bequeathed to three hundred dirhams. Then whatever remains after that is theirs.”

I said: “What if the one for whom the bequest was made dies?” He said: “If he dies, the three hundred dirhams belong to his heirs; they inherit it so long as any one of them remains. Then when his heirs come to an end and none of them remains, the three hundred dirhams belong to the relatives of the deceased, returned to what comes forth from the endowment, then divided among them; they inherit that so long as any one of them remains and the yield remains.”

I said: “Do the heirs from the relatives of the deceased have the right to sell the land if they need it and what comes from the yield is not enough for them?” He said: “Yes, if all of them agree and the sale is better for them, they may sell.”

key_terms.أَوْصَى: He made a bequest or testamentary designation.
key_terms.الْبَيْعُ: The sale of the land when agreed upon and beneficial.
key_terms.الْوَقْفِ: The endowment itself as a dedicated charitable holding.
key_terms.غَلَّةً: The produce or yield generated from the endowed property.
key_terms.قَرَابَةٍ: Relatives or kin from the designated family lines.
key_terms.وَرَثَتِهِ: His heirs who inherit after him.
key_terms.وَقَفَ: He endowed property as a waqf.

ai.seo_question: How is the yield of a waqf distributed when a fixed annual bequest was assigned to someone outside the family?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on an endowment whose yield is distributed between relatives and a non-relative beneficiary named in a bequest. It establishes that the specified annual amount for the bequeathed recipient takes priority from the yield, then the remainder goes to the relatives, and it also explains how that right passes to heirs and when sale of the land is permitted.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5577 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Ja'far ibn Hanan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as), about a man who endowed the yield of his property for his relatives from his father's side and his mother's side.
He also made a bequest for a man and his descendants - who had no relation to him - to receive three hundred dirhams annually from that yield, with the remainder to be distributed among his relatives from both his father's and mother's sides.
Imam (as) said: "It is permissible for the one to whom he made that bequest."

I then asked: "What if the yield from the endowed land is only five hundred dirhams?"
Imam (as) replied: "Is it not in his will that the one he designated should receive three hundred dirhams from the yield, and the remainder be divided among his relatives from his father's and mother's sides?"

I said: "Yes."
Imam (as) replied: "His relatives have no right to take anything from the yield until the bequested three hundred dirhams are fully given to the one it was intended for. After that, whatever remains belongs to them."

I asked: "What if the person for whom the bequest was made dies?"
Imam (as) said: "If he dies, the three hundred dirhams will go to his heirs, and they will inherit it as long as any of them remain. If his heirs perish and none remain, the three hundred dirhams will revert to the relatives of the deceased (the original owner) and will be distributed from the yield of the endowment among them, and they will continue to inherit it as long as any of them remain, while the yield itself will continue."

I asked: "Do the heirs from the deceased's relatives have the right to sell the land if they are in need and the yield does not suffice for them?"
Imam (as) replied: "Yes, if all of them agree and the sale is better for them, then they may sell it."
